notes.1d: (i) This was generally well known but candidates often didn't gain credit as they omitted the lone pairs on the sulfur and the four fluorine atoms. Some candidates incorrectly drew one or more dative bonds.

notes.1f: (i) Most candidates gained credit. Common incorrect responses included from car exhausts and from sulfide ores rather than from roasting sulfide ores.

notes.2a: Many correct calculations were seen, but a significant number of candidates did not quote their answer to two decimal places and so did not gain full credit. �PAGE�31
notes.2b: (i) Many candidates did not make a comparison so both being amphoteric or acidic or basic were common responses. Some candidates answered in terms of the relative stabilities or redox capabilities of Sn(II) and Sn(IV) which were not creditworthy.
notes.2bii: Some candidates showed incorrectly both oxides reacting as acids or bases. A number of candidates gave the products of SnO2 reacting with HCl incorrectly as SnCl 2 + Cl 2.

notes.3a: The majority of candidates correctly calculated the mass number and charge but a significant number did not give the correct symbol. S, Cl and As were commonly seen.
notes.3b: The majority of candidates gained full credit. Common incorrect responses included the solubility becoming more endothermic rather than ∆Ho sol and that the enthalpy change of hydration decreased less rapidly.
notes.3c: Many candidates described seeing a white precipitate, but fewer identified it correctly. Common identities included CaO, Ca(OH)2, Ca, Na2O, Na. Most gained credit for the explanation.
notes.3d: Many candidates gained full credit and some gained partial credit for their working. However, some candidates who ended up with an incorrect answer did not show their working clearly enough to gain any credit.
notes.4a: (i) Many candidates thought incorrectly that a buffer solution maintains pH or keeps pH constant. Some candidates didn't appreciate that only small amounts of acid or alkali are added.
notes.4aii: Most candidates gained credit for the reaction of the HCO3 with acid but fewer gave a correct equation with OH .
notes.4iii: This buffer calculation proved difficult for some candidates. The most common incorrect responses included reversing the acid/base ratio or using the concentration of Na2HPO4 as 0.2 mol dm .
notes.4b: (i) Several candidates either omitted the charges on the ions or gave incorrect charges mainly Ag and PO4 , or omitted the cubic index. Some split the PO4 into P and 4 × O. In general the units fitted the expressions.
notes.4bii: Many candidates answered very well here. Commonly candidates did not multiply the [PO4 ] in their K sp calculation by 3, in order to get the [Ag + ]. Some expanded (3x) 3 as 3x 3 or 9x 3 , rather than = 27x .
notes.4c: Several candidates either could not balance the equation, often including electrons on the left or the right hand side, or reversed the equation. Most calculated the correct cell although +0.49 V was a common incorrect response.

notes.key_messages:
The rubric requires answers to be written in ink, the use of pencils by candidates in writing formulae,
structures and equations is to be strongly discouraged. Pencilled text is sometimes too faint to read and also
some candidates write over the pencil in ink so that their answers become illegible.
notes.general_comments:
The paper differentiated well, with no evidence of candidates being short of time.
Candidates need to show their working in mathematical questions, where a final answer is incorrect often
credit can be obtained from correct working.
There was evidence, even from some stronger candidates, of incorrect bond connectivity, 3- and 5-valent
carbon atoms and formulae errors such as CO3 and PO4 .
